EC→EO centered-shape deviation: one bounded experiment (closed)

Exploratory follow-up (DEVIATION_PROTOCOL.md, frozen before any shape diagnostic or remission scoring). The learned reference structure is real and the deviations are reliable within a session, but they do not predict remission: candidate D failed the frozen funding rule (mean AUC 0.503; gain over E01c -0.074), so this resting-power extension is closed. Better reconstruction alone did not establish reliable or predictive deviations, and reliable deviations did not establish prediction. Limitations preserved: same 164 patients already used four times; session 1 = pretreatment assumed (unverified); v2 cleaning has unresolved removals (drift-like and no-eye-evidence components) and 8 ICA failures.

Three claims, kept distinct

QuestionEvidenceAnswer
1. Learned reference structureShape ridge cuts held-out MSE 42% below the stronger trivial baseline (persistence + mean shift); uncentered ridge cuts MSE 56% below an amplitude-only predictor.Yes (reference people only; previously examined evaluation set)
2. Reliable deviationsMedian split-half SB 0.85 (all 12 lower bounds ≥ 0.70); the simple contrast is as reliable (0.87).Yes within a recording session (halves of the same recording; not test-retest across days)
3. Remission predictionD (levels + deviation) mean Remitter AUC 0.503 [0.423, 0.587]; gain over E01c -0.074 [-0.171, +0.028]; permutation p = 0.417No. Funding rule not met; extension closed.
4. Does the learned reference add beyond levels / simple contrast?D minus A +0.046 [-0.047, +0.142]; D minus C +0.010 [-0.031, +0.049]Not supported (frozen rule requires funding AND ≥+0.05 with positive repeats and an interval excluding 0 versus each)

1. Mapping against stronger baselines (reference people; follow-up on an already examined set)

Identity check: the re-fitted uncentered mapping reproduces the previous stage exactly (alpha 1, mean R² 0.805). Level (overall amplitude) carries 63% of the total across-person variance of the 12 EO log powers (shape the remaining 37%), and EC and EO levels correlate 0.87; the earlier R² of 0.805 was therefore largely a shared level, yet the uncentered ridge still beats amplitude-only by 56% MSE.

3. Reference applicability

Included reference people (762 of 1023) differ from excluded ones (missing EC/EO features): excluded people are much younger (median age 21 vs 44) with fewer clean windows (EC median 18 vs 57); the reference is therefore a cleaner, adult-skewed subset. Patients (median age 46, 51% female) resemble reference-training (median age 44, 48% female). Missingness: 11 of 164 patients have an incomplete EC or EO vector (EC 2, EO 10) versus 26% of reference people. The reference mixes diagnoses (workbook-HEALTHY is a minority) and is a population reference, not a healthy norm; diagnoses and demographics were not used as predictors.

4. Remission models (A, B, C, D) against saved E01c

Frozen decision rules. Funding (D vs E01c): mean AUC ≥ 0.60 (D 0.503), gain ≥ +0.05 (-0.074), positive in every repeat (False): not met. Learned-reference-helps claim: not supported. Permutation (chance association of D only, 999 permutations, rng seed 21, folds regenerated from permuted labels, full refit, plus-one): observed 0.503, null mean 0.488, 95th percentile 0.585, p = 0.417; not a test of incremental value or superiority.

Limits and reproduction

  • Same 164 patients, previously used; bootstrap intervals are conditional on saved predictions and exclude training/tuning uncertainty; no multiplicity correction is claimed.
  • Session-1 timing unverified; v2 cleaning has unresolved removals and ICA failures; levels may contain measurement effects.
  • Reference evaluation set was already examined; reliability is within-session; the reference is a mixed-diagnosis, cleaner, adult-skewed population.
  • Models A–D use 2–24 features; E01c (65 features, corrected cleaning) remains the highest-scoring Remitter model (see table) but is itself not above chance by its own interval.

Reproduce (from first_tests/): scripts/30_dev_window_powers.py; 29_dev_reference_mapping.py; 31_dev_reliability.py; 32_dev_applicability.py; 33_dev_outcomes.py; 34_dev_permutation.py; 35_dev_analysis.py; 36_dev_report.py (helpers: dev.py). Configs: runs/DEV_*/config.json, runs/DEVcc_*/config.json.
